## Initial Idea

**Raw Input:** `README.md`: a Bronze → Silver → Gold lakehouse on Microsoft Fabric built from the Fruit Juice dataset generated by `lab-sources`, with OneLake/Delta, Spark notebooks, Data Factory, Direct Lake, governance and `fabric-cicd`-based CI/CD. Status was "scaffold only".

Revised during the session: ingest **every** source `lab-sources` produces (CSV, Parquet, JSON, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MongoDB). The main complexity of the transformation layer is making all of them **converge to the same final data**. `lab-sources` is vendored into `sources/` and trimmed.

**Context Gathered:**
- The repo held only `README.md` and `.claude/` tooling: no code, no Git history, no IaC.
- `lab-sources` generates a seeded, byte-reproducible dataset for 2013–2026 at daily grain: 7 dimensions (6 static, plus `dim_tempo`) and 5 facts (sales 1.05M rows, freight 1.05M, fixed cost 10k, revenue target 1.02M, cost target 257k).
- Each source has its own quirks: CSV (all text), Parquet (hive `year=` partitions), JSON Lines (ISO date strings), SQL Server (T-SQL types), PostgreSQL (lower-cased identifiers), MongoDB (Extended JSON, lower-case fields, plus a denormalised `sales` collection with dimensions embedded).
- `dim_organizacional` is a nested-set hierarchy (`Esquerda`/`Direita`/`Nivel`). Codes are zero-padded strings (`COD_FABRICA = "002"`).
- **Done during the session:** `lab-sources` was vendored into `sources/` and trimmed. Removed: streaming/Kafka, the fitting code, the foundation originals, and the CLI period/seed/scale/format overrides. The six static dimension CSVs moved to `sources/src/reference/`. The config now emits all six formats by default. `uv run pytest`: 16 passed.

**Technical Context Observed (for Define):**

| Aspect | Observation | Implication |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| Likely Location | `sources/` (data generator, done); `workspace/` (Git-synced Fabric items); `notebooks/`, `pipelines/`, `warehouse/`, `semantic-model/`, `tests/`, `.github/workflows/` | Fabric items live in Git so the lab can be rebuilt after the trial expires |
| Relevant KB Domains | `microsoft-fabric` (medallion-fabric, lakehouse-vs-warehouse, copy-activity, incremental-load, direct-lake, star-schema, rls-security, purview-integration, git-integration, deployment-pipelines, deployment-rules), `medallion`, `lakehouse`, `data-modeling`, `data-quality`, `spark`, `sql-patterns`, `testing` | Patterns to consult in Define/Design |
| IaC Patterns | None. Docker Compose for the local source databases only | Fabric items deployed through `fabric-cicd` + Git integration; no Terraform |

**How samples will be used:**

- Canonical schema reference for the Silver adapters (column names, types, string codes)
- Test fixtures: a short generated period (e.g. 2013-01 to 2013-03) in all six formats, to unit-test adapters locally with PySpark
- Reconciliation ground truth: Gold totals per table and year vs the generated Parquet

## Approaches Explored

### Approach A: Lakehouse + Spark notebooks end-to-end

**Description:** Bronze, Silver and Gold are all Lakehouses. PySpark notebooks do every transform. Direct Lake runs on `lh_gold`.

**Pros:**
- Single engine and single test approach (local PySpark); most rebuildable
- Matches the KB `medallion-fabric` pattern (confidence 0.85: KB pattern, no codebase match)

**Cons:**
- Light on DP-600 Warehouse / T-SQL objectives

---

### Approach B: Lakehouse Bronze/Silver + Warehouse Gold ⭐ Selected

**Description:** Lakehouses for Bronze and Silver with PySpark notebooks. Gold is a Fabric **Warehouse** built with T-SQL (stored procedures, CTAS) that reads Silver through cross-database queries. The Direct Lake semantic model runs on the Warehouse.

**Pros:**
- Covers both engines: DP-700 Spark/pipelines and DP-600 Warehouse/T-SQL/modeling
- A clear portfolio story on choosing between a lakehouse and a warehouse (KB `lakehouse-vs-warehouse`, `hybrid-architecture`)

**Cons:**
- Two engines to test: PySpark for Silver, T-SQL for Gold reconciliation
- More items for `fabric-cicd` and the deployment pipeline to handle

**Why Selected:** The user chose it over the recommended A for cert breadth. The trade-off in testability was accepted.

---

### Approach C: Low-code (Dataflow Gen2 transforms)

**Description:** Pipelines plus Dataflow Gen2 (Power Query) for Silver and Gold.

**Pros:**
- Fast to build; covers Dataflow Gen2 exam objectives

**Cons:**
- Hard to review in Git and close to untestable; conflicts with the reconciliation requirement
- Heavy capacity unit use at ~1M rows per fact; weak engineering portfolio signal

## Data Engineering Context

### Source Systems

| Source | Type | Volume Estimate | Current Freshness |
|--------|------|-----------------|-------------------|
| CSV | Files (OneLake upload) | 250 MB, ~3.4M fact rows total | Static (regenerated on demand) |
| Parquet | Files (OneLake upload), hive `year=` | 30 MB | Static |
| JSON Lines | Files (OneLake upload) | 610 MB | Static |
| SQL Server 2025 | Database via gateway | ~3.4M fact rows | Static after `generator load` |
| PostgreSQL 17 | Database via gateway | ~3.4M fact rows | Static after `generator load` |
| MongoDB 8 | Database via gateway (⚠ connector to verify) | 1.4 GB export; `sales` 1.05M docs | Static after `generator load` |

### Data Flow Sketch

```text
sources/ (generator, seed 42)
 ├─ csv / parquet / json ──upload──▶ lh_bronze/Files/<source>/ ──▶ lh_bronze tables  brz_<source>_<table>
 └─ docker: sqlserver / postgres / mongo ──gateway + Copy activity──▶ lh_bronze tables  brz_<source>_<table>
                                                                        │  (native shape, + _source, _ingested_at, _batch_id)
                                                                        ▼
        lh_silver: per-source PySpark adapter ──▶ canonical schema per source ──▶ CONVERGENCE CHECK (6 sources identical)
                                                                        │  publish one canonical set
                                                                        ▼
        wh_gold (T-SQL): dim_* (SCD1, flattened org hierarchy) + fact_* ──▶ sm_fruitjuice (Direct Lake, RLS by region) ──▶ rpt_fruitjuice
                                                                        │
                                              RECONCILIATION TEST: Gold totals == generator output per table/year
```

### Key Data Questions Explored

| # | Question | Answer | Impact |
|---|----------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Expected data volume? | ~3.4M fact rows per source, ×6 sources in Bronze (~20M rows) | Fits a trial capacity comfortably; facts use incremental watermark on `DATA_FATO` |
| 2 | Freshness SLA? | None. Batch, on demand | Single orchestrating pipeline; no streaming |
| 3 | Who consumes the output? | Portfolio reviewers / the user for exam practice, through Power BI | Star schema + Direct Lake + one report; RLS by `Desc_Regiao` for demonstration |
| 4 | What defines "correct"? | All six sources converge to identical Silver; Gold reconciles to the generator | Convergence and reconciliation are first-class tests, not afterthoughts |

## Key Decisions Made

| # | Decision | Rationale | Alternative Rejected |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|
| 1 | Ingest all six `lab-sources` sources into Bronze, each in its native shape | The project's core skill is converging heterogeneous sources to one truth | Two paths only (files + SQL Server); one canonical source only |
| 2 | Silver = one PySpark adapter per source → one canonical schema, then a convergence check that all six are row-for-row identical | Makes "the final data looks the same" testable and visible | Picking one source as authoritative and ignoring the others |
| 3 | Gold in a Fabric Warehouse (T-SQL) reading Silver cross-database | DP-600 coverage; lakehouse-vs-warehouse story | Gold in a Lakehouse (Approach A) |
| 4 | Workspaces: `fruitjuice-dev` (Git-connected) + `fruitjuice-prod`, three items per layer (`lh_bronze`, `lh_silver`, `wh_gold`) | Demonstrates promotion with half the trial capacity of dev/test/prod | Dev/test/prod; one workspace per layer |
| 5 | Promotion split: `fabric-cicd` (GitHub Actions, service principal) deploys **Git → dev** and rebuilds after trial expiry; a Fabric **deployment pipeline** promotes **dev → prod** with deployment rules | Both are exam-relevant; separate jobs avoid conflict | Only one mechanism; Azure DevOps |
| 6 | Vendor `lab-sources` into `sources/`; trim streaming/Kafka, fitting code, foundation originals and CLI overrides; keep the 6 static dims in `src/reference/` | Self-contained repo; only what the lab uses (**done**, tests green) | Referencing `../lab-sources` as a sibling repo |
| 7 | Generated data is not committed; regenerated from seed 42 | 2.3 GB, byte-reproducible in ~2.5 min | Committing data files |
| 8 | Dimensions SCD1; facts incremental by `DATA_FATO` watermark, dims full reload | Source dims are static snapshots | SCD2 |

## Features Removed (YAGNI)

| Feature Suggested | Reason Removed | Can Add Later? |
|-------------------|----------------|----------------|
| Test environment (dev/test/prod) | Dev + prod is enough to show promotion and deployment rules; saves trial capacity | Yes |
| Dataflow Gen2 | Approach C rejected; pipelines + notebooks cover ingestion and transforms | Yes |
| Azure DevOps (alongside GitHub Actions) | One CI system | Yes |
| Streaming / Real-Time Intelligence; `generator stream` + Kafka | Out of scope for a batch medallion lab; code removed from `sources/` | Yes (restore from `lab-sources`) |
| SCD Type 2 dimensions | Source dims have no history | Yes |
| Refitting the model (`fit`, `export-original`, foundation originals) | Calibration JSON is committed; the lab never refits | Yes (restore from `lab-sources`) |
| Generator period/seed/scale/format CLI overrides | One fixed config (2013–2026, seed 42, all formats) | Yes |
| Fidelity-to-original checks in `validate` | Required the removed foundation tables; reconciliation is against generator output instead | Yes |
| Multiple reports / KPI marts | One report proves the semantic model | Yes |

**Kept after challenge** (user decision, exam objectives): Fabric deployment pipelines, RLS by region, Purview + OneLake security.

## Suggested Requirements for /define

### Problem Statement (Draft)

Build a reproducible Microsoft Fabric medallion lakehouse that ingests the same Fruit Juice dataset from six differently shaped sources and proves, through automated tests, that all of them converge to one identical Silver layer and a Gold star schema that reconciles exactly to the generated source data.

### Target Users (Draft)

| User | Pain Point |
|------|------------|
| The author (DP-700 / DP-600 candidate) | Needs hands-on coverage of Lakehouse, Warehouse, pipelines, gateway, Direct Lake, RLS, Purview, Git integration and deployment pipelines |
| Portfolio reviewers / hiring managers | Need a clear, runnable demonstration of multi-source integration, testing and CI/CD, not just screenshots |

### Success Criteria (Draft)

- [ ] All 12 tables from each of the 6 sources land in `lh_bronze` (72 Bronze tables), row counts equal to source
- [ ] Silver convergence check passes: the six canonical outputs are identical per table (row count, keys, measure sums; ideally a full-row hash)
- [ ] Gold reconciliation passes: `fact` row counts and `FATURAMENTO` / `IMPOSTO` / `CUSTO_VARIAVEL` / `FRETE` / `CUSTO_FIXO` / `META_*` totals per year equal the generated Parquet (e.g. `FATURAMENTO` = 2,664,425,394.54)
- [ ] Direct Lake model + one report show revenue, margin, freight and actual vs target; RLS by region verified with a test role
- [ ] A fresh workspace can be rebuilt from Git with `fabric-cicd` alone (trial-expiry test)
- [ ] dev → prod promotion through the deployment pipeline with deployment rules re-pointing item and connection IDs
- [ ] PySpark adapter unit tests run locally in CI on a short generated period

### Constraints Identified

- Fabric **trial** capacity: time-limited, so everything must be in Git and redeployable
- Database sources run in local Docker Compose and need an **on-premises data gateway** on the same machine
- ⚠ **MongoDB through the gateway** in Copy activity needs verifying in Design. Fallback: ingest the Extended-JSON export files (`data/mongodb/`) as the Mongo source
- Codes must stay strings (leading zeros); Postgres identifiers are lower-case; Mongo `sales` must be un-nested back to 001/002 + dims
- Generated data is not committed; Bronze loads depend on running `generator generate` / `load` first
- Python 3.11+, `uv`, `fabric-cicd`, service principal with workspace access

### Out of Scope (Confirmed)

- Streaming / Real-Time Intelligence / Kafka
- Dataflow Gen2
- Test environment (dev + prod only)
- Azure DevOps
- SCD2, multiple reports, KPI marts
- Refitting the generator model
